peak_detection.local_maximum: count strictly greater than left neighbor and greater than or equal to right neighbor on populated channels
peak_detection.merge_rule: When two maxima are closer than peak_min_separation channels, keep the taller; equal counts keep the lower channel

saturation_evidence.fwhm: Let half = floor(peak height / 2). From the peak channel walk left while the next populated channel holds a count strictly greater than half, and walk right on the same condition. fwhm is the outermost right channel minus the outermost left channel.
saturation_evidence.plateau: Contiguous run of channels whose counts are at least peak height minus saturation_plateau_delta; width includes the peak channel
saturation_evidence.exclusion: A peak is saturated when fwhm >= saturation_fwhm_min and plateau width >= saturation_plateau_min_width

calibration_fit.model: energy_mkeV = round_half_away_from_zero((slope_num * channel * intercept_den + intercept_num * slope_den) / (slope_den * intercept_den))
calibration_fit.method: Ordinary least squares on unsaturated matched line-peak pairs
calibration_fit.residual: residual_sum_sq_mkeV2 is the sum over included_lines of (line energy_mkeV - model energy at that line's matched peak channel) squared, evaluated with the model above.
calibration_fit.coefficients: slope and intercept as positive reduced fractions {num, den}

line_matching.rule: Sort calibration lines by energy_mkeV and peak candidates by channel; pair in order
line_matching.requirement: At least as many peak candidates as calibration lines
line_matching.line_match_max_delta: Each matched peak channel must lie within this many channels of the channel predicted by linear interpolation between the first and last paired line/peak endpoints using exact rational arithmetic and round_half_away

deadtime.correction: correction = total_span_us / live_time_us as a reduced fraction

integration.search: Within integration_half_width channels of the inverted calibration channel for each line, select the channel with maximum corrected_count as peak_channel. The inverted channel is the initial candidate and is replaced only by a strictly greater corrected_count, so ties keep the lowest channel.
integration.window: Sum corrected_count from peak_channel - integration_half_width through peak_channel + integration_half_width inclusive
integration.centroid: Count-weighted mean channel rounded with round_half_away_from_zero

json.jsonl: One compact sort-key-ordered JSON object per LF-terminated line.
